# ISLA and GeoTransolver, side by side; and what is new in ISLA {#sec-isla-vs-geotransolver}

**ISLA and GeoTransolver are the same kind of machine, a slice-attention
transformer, given different things to see, and the standing between them
has one shape: ISLA is the more accurate or the only usable model wherever
the evaluation departs from the training conventions, ISLA leads or ties
at lower cost on geometry-varying tasks, and GeoTransolver leads on small
training sets, on the small wing rungs and on the solids' tensor
targets.** The departures from the training conventions are pose,
sampling draw, sampling law and the range of a global condition. On
geometry-varying tasks ISLA leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width or
ties its parameter match at lower cost, and leads on most field
quantities. On the fixed-mesh boundary-data problems ISLA leads on the
scalar Poisson set and trails on the elasticity tensor. This appendix steps back from the chapter-by-chapter
evidence and reads the whole standing in one table and one figure. It then
asks the question a paper must answer: which of ISLA's ideas are new,
which are adopted, and which are worth telling others about. It ends with
the ideas from the literature that the comparison says we should try.
Nothing here restates a chapter's argument. Every row points to the
chapter that holds the study, and every number is computed from the
artifact the chapter cites. Ratios are baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring
ISLA. The metric is the area-weighted relative L2 in float32 (@sec-metrics)
under the reporting protocol (@sec-protocol) unless a row says otherwise.

```{python}
#| label: setup-vs
#| include: false

from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
FIELDS = ("pressure_l2", "velocity_l2", "nut_l2"); FNAME = {"pressure_l2": "pressure", "velocity_l2": "velocity", "nut_l2": "eddy viscosity"}

# --- ISLA is the reference configuration (384 x 12, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4) -----------------------------
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
refm = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["mean"]
# --- surface accuracy, DrivAerML Surface task ---------------------------------------------------------------
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
isla435 = refm("isla_r1|dr435"); gt512_435 = refm("gt_w512|dr435")
gt435 = min(P2["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["pressure_mean"], P2["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"])
RBS = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
lad = {n: min(RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"]["mean"], RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]["mean"]) / RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["mean"] for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
# --- surface accuracy, HiLiftAeroML rungs (the 35-case rung is the reference configuration; the others the earlier protocol) ---
W35 = refm("isla_r1|hl35")
F20 = J("p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json")["datasets"]; F22 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json")["datasets"]
def gt_best(d):
    a = d["arms"]; c = {k: a[k]["pressure_l2_mean"] for k in ("gt_unit", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if k in a and a[k].get("n_evaluated")}
    return min(c.values())
gt35 = gt_best(F22["highlift_surface_super_scarce"])
WING = {
    "35 random cases": (gt35, W35),
    "210 random cases": (gt_best(F22["highlift_surface_scarce"]), F22["highlift_surface_scarce"]["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_mean"]),
    "4 geometries (never-seen validation geometries)": (gt_best(F20["highlift_surface_geometry_super_scarce"]), F20["highlift_surface_geometry_super_scarce"]["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_mean"]),
    "21 geometries (never-seen validation geometries)": (gt_best(F22["highlift_surface_geometry_scarce"]), F22["highlift_surface_geometry_scarce"]["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_mean"]),
    "126 geometries at a fixed 12°": (gt_best(F20["highlift_surface_single_aoa_12"]), F20["highlift_surface_single_aoa_12"]["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_mean"]),
}
wing_ratio = {k: g / i for k, (g, i) in WING.items()}
# --- interior: DrivAerML Volume task and AirfRANS ----------------------------------------------------------
VG = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]["gt_vol_unit"]
vol = {f: VG[f]["mean"] / refm("isla_r1|drvol", f) for f in FIELDS}
AF = J("airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json")
af = {f: AF["arms"]["gt_volume_1e-3"][f]["mean"] / refm("isla_r1|af", f) for f in FIELDS}
AFX = J("airfrans_extrap_2026-09-22.json")["splits"]
afx_on = {sp: {f: AFX[sp]["gt_over_isla_on_split"][f]["mean"] for f in FIELDS} for sp in ("reynolds", "aoa")}
afx_g = {sp: {f: AFX[sp]["growth"][f]["g_gt_over_g_isla"] for f in FIELDS} for sp in ("reynolds", "aoa")}
# --- solids and the fixed-mesh boundary-data sets ----------------------------------------------------------
SF = J("solids_frame_2026-09-22.json"); _LM = J("lane_means_2026-09-23.json")
T2 = {f: SF["summary"]["gt512|gt|n400"]["fields"][f]["mean"] / mean(_LM[f"v2_t2d_isla_r1_tensor_axis_n400_seed{s}"]["fields"][f] for s in (42, 43)) for f in ("sig11", "sig22", "sig12", "displacement")}  # tensor head + load axis at 400 cases
T2F = ("sig11", "sig22", "sig12", "displacement"); T2N = {"sig11": "σ11", "sig22": "σ22", "sig12": "σ12", "displacement": "displacement"}
LUG = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json"); LUGR = LUG["gt512_over_isla"]; LUGX = LUG["learning_curve_exponents"]
lug = {300: LUGR["isla_r1_lr25e4|n300"], 600: LUGR["isla_r1|n600"], 1200: LUGR["isla_r1|n1200"], 2400: LUGR["isla_r1|n2400"]}  # 300 at the half rate, as preregistered
# OLBC: current-snapshot ISLA references; the headline GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA at each rung is against the stronger of its two attention backends there
OLB = J("olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json")
def olbc_head(s, n, f):
    r = OLB[s][str(n)]; b = r.get("stronger_gt512"); x = r.get("gt512_over_isla", {}).get(b) if b else None
    return x["ratio"][f] if x else None
olbc_p = {n: olbc_head("poisson", n, "u_l2") for n in (512, 2048, 8448)}  # None until the rung is scored
olbc_e = {n: {f: olbc_head("elasticity", n, f + "_l2") for f in T2F} for n in (512, 2048)}  # rank-1 inputs + tensor output
olbc_scored = [n for n in (512, 2048, 8448) if olbc_p[n] is not None]
olbc_fmt = lambda x: f"{x:.2f}" if x is not None else "training"
olbc_ext512 = OLB["poisson"]["512"]["arms"].get("v7_extension", {}).get("ratio", {}).get("u_l2")  # the six-scalar inverse-square extension, arm ÷ reference (cross-snapshot)
# --- pose, draws, laws, territories -------------------------------------------------------------------------
PP = J("p200k_pose_r1_2026-09-23.json"); PV, PA = PP["verdict"], PP["arms"]
TAD = J("trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json"); TA = J("trainarea_reduction_2026-09-20.json")
WB = J("wingbench_200k_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
dens_cars = {m: TAD["arms"][f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]["biased"] / TAD["arms"][f"{m}_uniform"]["mean"]["unif"] for m in ("isla", "gt_unit")}
dens_wings = {"isla": WB["isla"]["mean"]["biased"] / WB["isla"]["mean"]["unif"], "gt_unit": WB["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["mean"]["biased"] / WB["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["mean"]["unif"]}
law_cars = {m: TAD["verdict"][f"{m}_area_over_uniform_unif"] for m in ("isla", "gt_unit")}
law_wings = {m: TA["verdict"][f"{m}_area_over_uniform_unif"] for m in ("isla", "gt_unit")}
TT = J("territory_2026-09-21.json")["models"]; TTW = J("territory_wings_2026-09-21.json")["models"]
disp = {"cars": (TT["ISLA"]["summary"]["displacement_median"], TT["GeoTransolver"]["summary"]["displacement_median"]),
        "wings": (TTW["ISLA"]["summary"]["displacement_median"], TTW["GeoTransolver"]["summary"]["displacement_median"])}
# --- learning-curve exponents ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLF = J("scalelaw_drivaerml_2026-09-22.json")["fits"]
alpha_dr = {m: (SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"]["fit"]["alpha"], SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"]["law_accepted_rms_below_3pct"]) for m in ("isla", "gt")}
AFS = J("airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json")["fits"]
alpha_af_isla = AFS["isla|pressure_l2"]["fit"]["alpha"]
alpha_af_gt_local = [v for k, v in AFS["gt|pressure_l2"]["local_alpha"].items() if int(k.split("-")[0]) >= 100]
# --- cost ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CS = J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"]
GIB_TO_GB = 1024 ** 3 / 1e9
at200 = {r["arm"]: r for r in CS if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
def cost(arm): r = at200[arm]; return statistics.median(r["step_ms"]), r["peak_allocated_gib"] * GIB_TO_GB, r["n_params"]
c_r1, c_g256, c_g512, c_i192 = cost("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"), cost("geotransolver_256"), cost("geotransolver_512"), cost("isla_192x12_cos_fused")
CAPI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
g1024 = CAPI["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]; i384 = CAPI["isla|w384|d12|s256|lr5e-4"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]; i384x24 = EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
def word(r, lo=0.98, hi=1.02):
    if r > hi: return f"ISLA leads by {pct(r)}"
    if r < lo: return f"GeoTransolver leads by {pct(r)}"
    return "parity within seed spread"
```

## What each is {#sec-vs-what}

**GeoTransolver** is the strongest public member of the Transolver family
(Wu et al., 2024; Adams et al., 2025): physics attention routes every
mesh point softly into a few hundred slices, attends among the slices, and
scatters the result back. It is handed coordinates centered on the sampled
points, the unit normal, and the problem's global vector. A geometry
encoder and a global-context projector condition every block on a
learned embedding of the whole shape. Its volume configuration
(GeoTransolver-volume) takes interior points as its tokens, each with the
signed distance to the full-resolution surface and that distance's
gradient, and never sees a surface sample. Nothing in it is equivariant or
sampling-consistent by construction. It learns pose, scale and the
mesher's habits from data, and does so well in distribution. What it sees,
and the protocol under which it is compared, are in @sec-part-baseline.

**ISLA** keeps the slice mechanism and changes what the network can see
(@sec-isla). No coordinate reaches a learned map. Every sum over the
boundary is a measure-weighted quadrature rule. Position is stated only as
invariants of a token against the slices' own anchors. The length unit is
the measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the sample. Vectors are
rebuilt once, at the output, from a basis that rotates with the body. The
forward pass with every tensor shape is @sec-architecture, and the
contracts it holds to roundoff are @sec-isla-contracts. Its general
boundary interface ($K$ global directions, $S$ global scalars, per-cell
boundary scalars, rank-1 boundary inputs and tensor outputs for component
targets, interior queries as tokens) is @sec-isla-inputs and @sec-arch-modes.

## Where ISLA is better and where it is worse {#sec-vs-standing}

```{python}
#| label: para-vs-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**Read across every axis the program has measured, the pattern is one sentence long: where the task varies the geometry, "
      f"ISLA leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width or ties its parameter match at lower cost, leads on the field quantities and "
      f"trails on small training sets; where the task varies only the boundary data on one fixed mesh, ISLA leads on the scalar "
      f"Poisson problem and trails on the elasticity tensor; and wherever the evaluation leaves the training conventions, ISLA is the "
      f"model whose error does not move.** At full "
      f"data on the DrivAerML Surface task ISLA leads GeoTransolver-256 by {pct(gt435 / isla435)} (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {gt435 / isla435:.2f}) "
      f"and ties the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512 ({gt512_435 / isla435:.2f}) at half its memory. Below full data GeoTransolver-256 "
      f"leads by {pct(lad[27])} at 27 cars and {pct(lad[54])} at 54, and ISLA leads from 109 cars up. On the HiLiftAeroML rungs "
      f"GeoTransolver leads by {pct(wing_ratio['35 random cases'])} at 35 cases and "
      f"{pct(wing_ratio['4 geometries (never-seen validation geometries)'])} at 4 geometries, shrinking to {pct(wing_ratio['21 geometries (never-seen validation geometries)'])} "
      f"where the validation geometries are never seen at 21 training geometries. On the interior ISLA leads on velocity by "
      f"{pct(vol['velocity_l2'])} (DrivAerML Volume task) and {af['velocity_l2']:.2f}x (AirfRANS). It leads on pressure by {pct(vol['pressure_l2'])} "
      f"on the cars and trails by {pct(af['pressure_l2'])} on the airfoils. Outside the AirfRANS training range it leads on every field. "
      f"On the solids GeoTransolver-512 leads ISLA by {pct(T2['sig11'])} to {pct(T2['displacement'])} on Tensile2d at 400 cases, and ISLA "
      f"leads on the lug ladder at the two small rungs and ties at the two large ones ({lug[300]:.2f} / {lug[600]:.2f} / {lug[1200]:.2f} / {lug[2400]:.2f} at 300 / 600 / "
      f"1,200 / 2,400 lugs). On the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set ISLA leads GeoTransolver-512 with no option at both scored rungs "
      f"({olbc_fmt(olbc_p[512])} at 512 cases and {olbc_fmt(olbc_p[2048])} at 2,048, each against the stronger of GeoTransolver's two attention "
      f"backends there), and on the OLBC elasticity set GeoTransolver-512 leads by {pct(max(olbc_e[512].values()))} to {pct(min(olbc_e[512].values()))} "
      f"at 512 cases. Under a 10:1 sampling bias ISLA's error moves {pct(dens_cars['isla'])} on the cars where GeoTransolver's grows "
      f"{dens_cars['gt_unit']:.1f}x. Trained under the other sampling law ISLA moves {pct(law_wings['isla'])} and {pct(law_cars['isla'])} "
      f"where GeoTransolver degrades {law_wings['gt_unit']:.1f}x and {law_cars['gt_unit']:.1f}x. In arbitrary poses ISLA leads the "
      f"rotation-augmented GeoTransolver by {pct(PV['gt_aug_posed_over_isla_posed'])}. @tbl-vs-standing carries every axis with its anchor.")
```

```{python}
for r in rows: out += "| " + " | ".join(r) + " |\n"
print(out)

      "Seeds, paired counts, rates and controls are in the chapter each row cites; every cell holds two seeds. How to read this: rows are different instruments and are not comparable with one another; the table ranks nothing, it locates. "
      "Data: results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json, refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json, p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json, p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json, "
      "p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json, ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json, routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json, airfrans_extrap_2026-09-22.json, "
      "solids_frame_2026-09-22.json, solids_lug_2026-09-22.json, olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json, p200k_pose_r1_2026-09-23.json, trainarea_dr_reduction_2026-09-20.json, "
```

**The pattern.** Three things carry the table.

- **Geometry-varying tasks favor or tie ISLA once the training set is
  large enough, and the field quantities favor it earlier.** At full data
  on the cars the two are indistinguishable, and both reach the same
  capacity floor (@sec-shared-floor). On the interior ISLA's velocity lead
  is the largest cross-architecture margin in the book on two datasets and
  two PDE regimes, and outside the AirfRANS training range it leads on
  every field, pressure included (@sec-interior-extrapolation). Its costs
  are at the bottom of the data ladders: the small car rungs, the small
  wing rungs where validation geometries recur in training, the first rung
  of the lug ladder. The learning-curve exponents say why the two readings
  are one. On the three datasets where the exponents differ (AirfRANS,
  Tensile2d, the lug), ISLA's is the larger, so GeoTransolver's small-data
  lead is an offset that the ladder erodes. On DrivAerML the exponents are
  the same and the offset is gone at 435 cars. The boundary-first
  representation is the data-hungrier one at the bottom of a ladder and
  the steeper one along it.
- **Fixed-mesh boundary-data tasks split by target.** On the OLBC sets
  the geometry is identical in every sample and the whole signal is in
  per-cell boundary scalars and a nodal source (@sec-data-olbc). On the
  scalar Poisson problem ISLA leads GeoTransolver-512 at both scored rungs
  with no option, against the stronger of GeoTransolver's two attention
  backends at each rung; on the elasticity tensor GeoTransolver-512 leads
  on every field at both rungs. The per-type geometry channels tested
  there are neutral or worse on Poisson and cost at 512 elasticity cases,
  so none is part of the model (@sec-interior-olbc). Elasticity is the
  axis on which the ordering runs the other way from the rest of the
  book, together with Tensile2d: both are tensor targets on solids.
- **Consistency is ISLA's, and it is a property of the frame plus the
  measure, not of the attention.** Under the biased inference draw, under
  the swapped training law and in arbitrary poses ISLA's error moves by
  percent where GeoTransolver's moves by factors, on two datasets each. Its
  slice anchors stay put under a change of draw where GeoTransolver's
  centroids travel two thirds of a body radius. The ablations that add
  ISLA's measure weights and a Horvitz–Thompson center to GeoTransolver
  recover its consistency (@sec-robustness-density). That locates the
  mechanism and also says it is portable. The released baselines are not
  modified, so it reaches users through ISLA (@sec-principled-decisions).
  The memory advantage is real and useful (half the memory at parity
  against the parameter match) and is not what the architecture is for.

Open on this page: the two largest HiLiftAeroML rungs, the OLBC 8,448-case
rung and the current-snapshot elasticity references, the DeepJEB equal-epoch companion, third seeds of the
interior standing, and the reference-configuration re-run of every evidence
lane (@sec-program-status).

## Novel contributions of ISLA beyond the state of the art {#sec-vs-novel}

**Of ISLA's eight candidate ideas, three are new in the sense a paper
needs (no prior work does them, and the book has evidence they matter),
three are adoptions with a new diagnosis or a new setting attached, and
two are engineering.** Each is stated as the idea in one sentence, the
closest prior work, what is genuinely new, the evidence, and whether it is
worth writing up. The literature this rests on is summarized in
@sec-vs-bibliography; sources that could not be read in full are marked
there.

### (a) An origin-free frame with an integral length unit {#sec-vs-novel-frame}

*The idea.* No center is ever named: positions enter only as differences
against the slices' own anchors, and the one length unit is the
measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the sample, a two-point integral
that converges under refinement even where the total measure does not
(@sec-isla-frame).

*Closest prior work.* Translation invariance through relative positions is
the standard construction of equivariant message passing: EGNN builds its
messages from relative squared distances and updates coordinates as
weighted sums of relative vectors (Satorras et al., 2021); MeshGraphNets
encode relative positions on edges (Pfaff et al., 2021); MP-PDE carries
relative positions in its messages (Brandstetter et al., 2022). All of them
take differences between *neighbors* on a graph. Frame Averaging (Puny et
al., 2022) and learned canonicalization (Kaba et al., 2023) instead center
on a centroid and align to principal axes, which is what the canonical
frame of @sec-pose does for GeoTransolver. Point-cloud practice normalizes
each cloud to a unit sphere or a per-dataset constant length; the recipe's
GeoTransolver uses a per-dataset reference length.

*What is new.* The reference points are not neighbors and not a centroid
but the data-adaptive anchors of a global slice partition, so a
transformer with no neighborhoods and no positional encoding is exactly
translation-invariant; and the length unit is chosen for its estimator
properties (measure-weighted, center-free, normalized so a rescale of the
weights alone is invisible, finite on a Koch curve). Neither piece is
deep; the combination is what lets a slice transformer be handed no
coordinate at all.

*Evidence.* The contracts (@sec-isla-contracts); the biased-draw and
training-law results and the ablation that gives GeoTransolver a
Horvitz–Thompson center and recovers its consistency
(@sec-robustness-density), which shows the frame is the load-bearing
part; the length-unit decision row (@sec-principled-ledger).

*Publication-worthy?* As a component of the architecture paper, yes, with
the ablation as its argument; not on its own.

### (b) A scalar trunk on invariants of the per-point vector set, and a vector head from an equivariant basis {#sec-vs-novel-invariants}

*The idea.* Every learned map sees only norms and dot products of the
vectors a token has (its separation from an anchor, its normal, the
anchor's normal, the global directions); vectors are rebuilt once at the
output as invariant coefficients times body-fixed directions
(@sec-isla-relational, @sec-isla-heads).

*Closest prior work.* "Scalarize, compute on invariants, vectorize with a
local frame" is the ClofNet construction (Du et al., 2022) and, in
spirit, GemNet's distance-angle-dihedral invariants (Gasteiger et al.,
2021); PaiNN keeps a separate vector stream (Schütt et al., 2021); Vector
Neurons lift every neuron to a 3-vector (Deng et al., 2021); Tensor Field
Networks, SE(3)-Transformers, Equiformer and e3nn carry irreducible
representations through every layer (Thomas et al., 2018; Fuchs et al.,
2020; Liao and Smidt, 2023; Geiger and Smidt, 2022); GATr carries the
projective geometric algebra (Brehmer et al., 2023) and has been applied
to arterial wall shear stress. GLOBE (Sharpe, 2025) builds a
translation-, rotation- and parity-equivariant surrogate from
Green's-function-like kernels evaluated from boundary faces to targets. All
of these are equivariant; most pay for it inside every layer.

*What is new.* The choice to keep the *entire* transformer trunk an
ordinary scalar network and pay for equivariance once at the edges, in an
industrial-scale slice transformer, and the result that this costs
nothing in accuracy or in step time at the reporting protocol
(@sec-scoreboard-200k, @sec-cost-sweep). The contrast in the literature is
sharp. The E(3)-equivariant AB-GATr of Rygiel et al. (2026) is reported
to trail its non-equivariant twin in distribution on aligned car data
(6.31% against 4.81% pressure error on ShapeNet-Car as they report it) at
about three times the training time and three times the memory of AB-UPT.
That is the accepted price of full-tensor equivariance. ISLA's price is
zero at parity. A second new element is small and crisp. Scalar heads
on invariants are reflection-invariant, so a frame-component target
(a stress $\sigma_{12}$, a laboratory-axis displacement) is representable
only as a view of a predicted tensor, and $\sigma_{12}$ is
unrepresentable by a scalar head with a single axis (@sec-isla-heads). No
prior work we read states this clause, and every aerodynamic benchmark
hides it. A third element is a rule rather than a mechanism: every input
ISLA takes is a datum of the PDE problem (geometry, boundary data,
parameters, load and body-force directions), and the dataset's own axes
are refused even where they buy accuracy (@sec-pose-prior).

*Evidence.* The contracts; the pose result against augmentation
(@sec-pose-contract); the full-data standing (a lead over the recipe
width, parity with the parameter match, @sec-scoreboard-200k) and the
shared capacity floor (@sec-shared-floor); the Tensile2d tensor-head lanes (@sec-interior-tensile2d,
@sec-nb-solids-frame-interim); the pose-prior diagnostic (@sec-pose-prior).

*Publication-worthy?* Yes: "exact SE(3) covariance at zero accuracy and
zero time cost in a slice transformer" is a statement the equivariance
literature does not currently have, and the component clause is a
reusable warning. Honest scope: the covariance itself is not new; the
price is.

### (c) Measure-weighted slice routing, and discretization consistency as the acceptance criterion {#sec-vs-novel-measure}

*The idea.* The routing softmax over points carries the log cell measure
as a bias, so every slice state is a quadrature estimate of a surface
integral and inherits Horvitz–Thompson consistency under any sampling law
(@sec-isla-quadrature); a change to the architecture is adopted only if
the prediction converges to one field under refinement and to the same
field under two sampling laws (@sec-principle).

*Closest prior work.* Neural operators are defined by discretization
invariance in the fine-mesh limit (Kovachki et al., 2023), and the kernel
integral of the graph neural operator is a quadrature sum (Li et al.,
2020). Cao (2021) read attention as a kernel integral and proposed
Galerkin-style normalization; Berner et al. (2025) state the general
recipe explicitly, quadrature weights in the normalization and aggregation
of attention so that the layer has a unique limit under refinement; IPOT
(Lee and Oh, 2024) and LNO (Wang and Wang, 2024) decouple discretization
from processing through inducing points and latent tokens. Transolver and
GeoTransolver do not weight their slices by cell measure (the GeoTransolver
implementation in this tree carries an optional `measure_weighted_slices`
switch that is off in the public model; @sec-part-baseline). M³ (Mei et
al., 2026) identifies the biased empirical measure induced by mesh
discretization as a *training* problem and rebalances supervision across
space. RIGNO and GAOT report robustness to unseen resolutions (Mousavi et
al., 2025; Wen et al., 2025).

*What is new.* Three things. The form: a log-measure bias inside the
point-softmax of slice routing, which makes a soft partition a set of
quadrature rules without changing anything else in the layer. The
instruments: a biased inference draw with exact inclusion weights, a
training-law swap scored on an independent draw, a convergence benchmark
across three samplers, and a territory probe of where the slices sit.
Together they turn "discretization-invariant" from an asymptotic
property claimed by construction into a measured, preregistered readout.
And the finding: the two released slice transformers depend on
the sampling law by factors of 2.4 to 9.6 on two datasets. No
benchmark had exposed this, because every benchmark samples the way it trains.

*Evidence.* @sec-robustness-density, @sec-training-law,
@sec-consistency-bench, @sec-territories; the weights-off ablation row
(@sec-principled-ledger); the anatomy of the cell-count gap, which is the
price (@sec-deficit-anatomy).

*Publication-worthy?* Yes, and it is the strongest candidate: the
instruments and the finding stand on their own as a benchmark paper, and
the mechanism is a one-line change any slice transformer can adopt.
Honest scope: quadrature-weighted attention is adopted from the
neural-operator literature; the routing form, the instruments and the
factors are new.

### (d) Soft anchors and point-to-anchor invariants as the positional encoding {#sec-vs-novel-anchors}

*The idea.* Each slice forms, from its own routing weights, a mean
position and a mean normal; every token's position is then a handful of
invariant scalars per anchor, which refine the routing and are pooled
back into the token (@sec-isla-slices, @sec-isla-relational).

*Closest prior work.* Soft assignment of many inputs to a few latent
tokens is Transolver's slice (Wu et al., 2024), Perceiver's latent array
(Jaegle et al., 2021), Set Transformer's inducing points (Lee et al.,
2019), UPT's supernodes (Alkin et al., 2024) and Slot Attention's slots,
whose softmax runs over slots so that slots compete for inputs and each
slot is a weighted mean (Locatello et al., 2020). In every one of these
the latent token is a weighted mean of *features*; the positions of the
inputs are consumed as features too. GeoTransolver's GALE attention
cross-attends every block to a shared geometry embedding (Adams et al.,
2025). Hu et al. (2025) show physics attention is a form of linear
attention whose value lies in the slice and deslice operations rather
than in inter-slice interaction.

*What is new.* Anchors as *geometric* aggregates (position and normal)
that rotate with the body, and the use of a token's relation to that
constellation as its only knowledge of where it is: a data-adaptive,
equivariant, coordinate-free positional encoding. We found no prior work
that forms slice positions and uses them this way. The trained partitions
of @sec-arch-routing-trained are the picture of it.

*Evidence.* Removing the relational invariants from routing and read-back
is the largest single-factor effect measured (@sec-de-limits); the
territory probe shows the anchors are functions of the surface
(@sec-territories). The bound on the mechanism is as important: on a
fixed mesh the anchors barely move between samples, so positional
resolution is only as fine as the partition; yet on the OLBC Poisson set
ISLA leads GeoTransolver-512 at both scored rungs with no positional
channel added, so 256 anchors resolve that problem (@sec-interior-olbc).

*Publication-worthy?* Yes, as the core mechanism of the architecture
paper, stated with the fixed-mesh bound and the OLBC evidence.

### (e) Cosine routing against slice collapse {#sec-vs-novel-cosine}

*The idea.* The routing logit is a temperature times the cosine between
the normalized token state and a learned prototype per slice, so every
logit is bounded and no block can route every point to one slice
(@sec-isla-routing-forms).

*Closest prior work.* Scaled cosine attention in Swin Transformer V2
replaces the dot product because in large models the attention maps of
some blocks become dominated by a few pixel pairs (Liu et al., 2022);
QK-normalization L2-normalizes queries and keys against softmax
saturation (Henry et al., 2020). Transolver++ addresses the *opposite*
failure of slice weights, their becoming uniform so that attention
degenerates to average pooling, with a per-point adaptive temperature and
a Gumbel-softmax reparameterization (Luo et al., 2025). Load-balancing
losses in sparse expert routing exist for the same family of failure
(Fedus et al., 2022).

*What is new.* Not the fix but the diagnosis. The mean-field plateau of
linear-routed ISLA was measured to be total routing collapse (one active
slice per block, all anchors coincident), with a learning-rate ceiling
that falls like one over the width and at least one over the depth.
Bounding the logits removes it at neutral or better accuracy on two
datasets (@sec-nb-routingsat-verdict, @sec-nb-routenorm-p200k-verdict).
Whether the released Transolver family shares the ceiling is untested
(GeoTransolver degrades several-fold at a rate of 1e-2 on the cars, from
an earlier exploration-budget grid, mechanism unmeasured).

*Evidence.* @sec-isla-routing-forms and its dropdown table; the design
row (@sec-principled-ledger).

*Publication-worthy?* As a section: "adopted from Swin V2 and QK-norm;
the collapse mechanism and the width-depth rate law are the
contribution." It becomes more if the same ceiling is shown in
GeoTransolver.

### (f) The general boundary interface {#sec-vs-novel-interface}

*The idea.* One model reads $K$ global unit directions, $S$ global scalars,
per-cell boundary scalars, rank-1 boundary inputs and tensor outputs for
component targets, and interior queries as interacting tokens, and the same class trains on
cars, wings, airfoils, a tensile specimen, a lug and a fixed-mesh
Poisson problem (@sec-isla-inputs, @sec-arch-modes).

*Closest prior work.* GNOT's heterogeneous normalized attention takes
multiple input functions, geometries and parameters through cross
attention with a geometric gate (Hao et al., 2023); BENO embeds boundary
geometry and inhomogeneous boundary values through two GNN branches and a
transformer over the boundary, with a Green's-function motivation (Wang
et al., 2024); GINOT feeds loading conditions beside the surface point
cloud and decodes queries by attention (Liu et al., 2025); MP-PDE puts
boundary conditions and PDE parameters in the messages; Mousavi et al.
(2026) extend boundary data into the domain as a learned pseudo-field so
that any domain-to-domain operator can consume it, and build the OLBC
benchmark to test exactly this.

*What is new.* The typed contract: directions enter as unit vectors and
magnitudes as scalars for every model (@sec-unit-direction-rule), a
component target is a view of a tensor output, every input is a datum of
the PDE problem, and every channel keeps the covariance contracts under test. That is interface design, not a
mechanism.

*Evidence.* The contract tests; the unit-direction control on the
baselines; the Tensile2d tensor-head lanes; the OLBC sets, where the
boundary data enter through this interface alone (@sec-interior-olbc).

*Publication-worthy?* The component clause, yes (it belongs with (b)); the
interface as a whole is an engineering contribution to the code, not a
paper.

### (g) The boundary-first learning curve and the extrapolation crossover {#sec-vs-novel-curves}

*The idea.* A model that sees only the boundary, as invariants, is
data-hungrier at the bottom of a ladder and steeper along it, and
degrades less when a global condition leaves its training range.

*Closest prior work.* Scaling laws for neural operators and surrogates
exist as within-architecture fits: Subramanian et al. (2023) for FNO
across PDE systems, Setinek et al. (2025) for multi-fidelity CFD
surrogates, AB-UPT's within-family scaling (Alkin et al., 2025). Rygiel et
al. (2026) find that equivariance helps most on small and diverse
hemodynamic datasets and that "increased data alone does not reliably
replace symmetry-aware structure", a data-efficiency reading in the
opposite direction from ours. We found no cross-architecture comparison
of learning-curve exponents on industrial CFD.

*What is new.* The measurement itself: on four datasets the exponents are
the same on one (DrivAerML) and larger for ISLA on three (AirfRANS,
Tensile2d, the lug), with the OLBC ladders pending their third rung; and
the AirfRANS extrapolation splits, where the in-distribution pressure
ordering inverts outside the training band (@sec-compute-allocation,
@sec-interior-tensile2d, @sec-interior-extrapolation). The mechanism is a
hypothesis, not a result: no probe has been run on those lanes.

*Publication-worthy?* Yes, as an empirical finding with its scope (four
datasets, two seeds, exponents fitted over at most five rungs), and the
most interesting thing to a reader who already has a surrogate; it needs
the OLBC ladder to land before it is stated as general.

### (h) The fused geometry kernel {#sec-vs-novel-kernel}

*The idea.* The per-layer geometry region (anchors, relational
invariants, refinement, pooling) is evaluated in one Triton kernel that
never materializes the $N{\times}M{\times}(5+K)$ tensor and recomputes it in
the backward pass (@sec-arch-layer, @sec-cost-sweep).

*Closest prior work.* Transolver-3 tiles the slice computation and
exploits associativity to reach 160-million-cell meshes (Zhou et al.,
2026); Transolver++ ships a parallelism framework for million-point
inputs; AB-UPT keeps attention quadratic on a reduced anchor set and
decodes the rest by cross attention. Activation recomputation is standard.

*What is new.* Nothing conceptually; the numbers are useful: with it, ISLA
tracks GeoTransolver's step at every token count in about half the memory
of its parameter match, and a 200,000-cell case that would not fit
otherwise does (@sec-cost-sweep).

*Publication-worthy?* As a systems paragraph in the architecture paper.

### What we would write a paper about {#sec-vs-ranked}

Ranked by how much of it is new and how much evidence stands behind it:

1. **Discretization consistency as a measured property of a surrogate,
   and the failure of the released slice transformers under a change of
   sampling law** (idea c): the instruments, the factors on two datasets,
   the one-line mechanism (a measure bias in the routing softmax) and its
   price. Self-contained, reproducible, and the result nobody has.
2. **Exact rigid-motion covariance at zero accuracy and zero time cost in
   a slice transformer** (ideas a, b, d together): the anchor-relative
   invariant construction, the full-data lead over the recipe width and
   parity with the parameter match at the capacity floor,
   the pose lead over augmentation, and the memory frontier; with the
   component clause of the scalar heads as its sharpest corollary.
3. **The boundary-first learning curve** (idea g): steeper exponents on
   three datasets and the extrapolation crossover, stated with the OLBC
   ladders once their third rung lands; the paper that a
   practitioner with a fixed budget would read.
4. **Routing collapse in slice attention and its removal** (idea e): a
   short, useful note, larger if GeoTransolver is shown to share the
   ceiling.
5. The general interface and the fused kernel (f, h): sections of the
   architecture paper, not papers.

## Ideas from the literature worth trying {#sec-vs-ideas}

**The review turned up eight experiments the comparison says we should
run; each targets a named weakness, has a smallest discriminating form,
and an acceptance bar written before it runs.** They are entered as
PLANNED nodes in the ledger of @sec-program-status (the LIT rows), so the
coordinating thread can schedule them.

| idea | source | ISLA weakness it targets | smallest discriminating experiment | acceptance bar | ledger row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boundary-value extension as a query scalar: give every interior query a fixed, parameter-free extension of the boundary data (a measure-weighted inverse-distance average of the prescribed values $g$ over the labeled cells, per condition type), so the value reaches the readout directly instead of only through the slices | Mousavi et al. (2026), learned function extensions; BENO's two-branch boundary embedding | a direct value path from the boundary data to the readout on the fixed-mesh sets | OLBC Poisson at 512 cases, the reference ISLA with the extension as rank-0 `query_inputs`, two seeds, against the reference configuration | run: the six-scalar extension scores `{python} olbc_fmt(olbc_ext512)` of the reference at 512 cases (arm ÷ reference, arm and reference on different code snapshots), so the value path through the slices is the better one; the row is closed (@sec-interior-olbc) | LIT-EXT |
| Per-token adaptive routing temperature (a learned $\tau_i$ added to the cosine form), the sharpness control of Transolver++ inside the bounded logit | Luo et al. (2025) | the too-soft wing routing (dominant-slice floors near 0.2 on the wings, @sec-territories) | the 35-wing rung at the reporting protocol and OLBC Poisson at 2,048 cases as the fixed-mesh control, two seeds | the wing rung improves by 5% or more on both seeds; OLBC Poisson within seed noise or better; the collapse-free property kept (every block above 4 active slices) | LIT-TEMP |
| Measure-weighted local aggregation among interior queries: a translation-invariant Gaussian kernel over query-to-query distances (the passive decoder's $\kappa$ of @sec-arch-passive-decoder, applied inside the interacting configuration) | GeoTransolver's multi-radius ball queries (Adams et al., 2025); DoMINO (Ranade et al., 2025); Erwin's ball-tree locality (Zhdanov et al., 2025); GAOT's multiscale encoders | the interior pressure deficit (13% cars, 17% airfoils); the notebook records query-to-query aggregation as the untested candidate after surface-patch features were falsified | DrivAerML Volume task at the reporting protocol, one kernel width in length units, two seeds; AirfRANS as the second dataset | pressure ratio from 0.95 to at least 1.00 with velocity moving by no more than 3%; falsified if pressure moves under 3% | LIT-LOCALQ |
| Parity-typed invariants: one reflection-odd relational scalar per anchor, the triple product $(\hat n_i \times \hat g_1) \cdot \hat\rho_{is}$, so scalar heads can represent pseudo-scalar components with a single global axis | GLOBE's parity-equivariance (Sharpe, 2025); GATr's typed algebra (Brehmer et al., 2023) | the $\sigma_{12}$ clause: unrepresentable with the load axis alone (@sec-isla-heads) | Tensile2d at 32 and 400 cases with the load axis $+y$ only, plus the odd scalar, two seeds, against the two-vector frame configuration | $\sigma_{12}$ within 1.5x of the frame configuration at both rungs with the other fields unchanged; scalar outputs stay exactly rotation-invariant (contract test) | LIT-PARITY |

: Ideas from the literature, each with the weakness it targets, its smallest discriminating experiment and its bar. How to read this: the bars are written before any of these runs; a row is not evidence of anything until its node is DONE in @sec-program-status. The last column is the node identifier in that chapter's ledger. {#tbl-vs-ideas}

Two ideas were considered and not entered. Query-independent decoding by
cross attention from the queries to a reduced anchor set (AB-UPT, UPT,
Perceiver IO) is the passive decoder the program already priced at
several-fold on every interior field. The interacting-support variant
that mirrors AB-UPT's anchors was measured too (@sec-arch-passive-decoder).
Canonicalization or frame averaging as an alternative to equivariance was
measured on GeoTransolver in @sec-pose and is the comparison the pose
contract is stated against.
